title: CAPDAG Capability Definition Schema
description: Schema for capability definitions across all language implementations

version.description: Per-definition version. Optional; absent ⇒ 0. v0 is the frozen pre-versioning state at the flat R2 path. v ≥ 1 is published at caps/<sha256>/<version>.json. Bumped explicitly in source TOMLs when content changes.

oneOf.description: Capability URN with tag-based format (deprecated - use string format)

tags.description: Key-value tags defining the capability. Must include 'in' (input spec ID) and 'out' (output spec ID) as required direction specifiers.

cap_description.description: Human-readable description of what this capability does

documentation.description: Optional long-form markdown documentation of this cap itself: what is specific to it. What the dims it was built from mean is documented once, with each dim (see `dims`), and is not repeated here; a reader shows both. Rendered in capability info panels, the cap navigator, capdag-dot-com, and anywhere else a rich-text explanation of the cap is useful. In TOML sources, author this as a triple-quoted literal string (''') so newlines and markdown punctuation pass through unchanged; the JSON generator re-escapes newlines per JSON rules on output.

dims.description: The dims this definition was built from, in the order its source references them: for each, the dim's name and the value chosen from it. A dim is published on its own (dim.schema.json) with its documentation and each value's; a reader shows that documentation beside this definition's own. The registry manifest says which version of each dim a snapshot holds. A dim appears at most once. Absent when the definition was built from no dim.

aliases.description: Globally-unique human-facing names that select this cap in the capdag CLI and the direct cartridge CLI. Replaces the former non-unique `command`.

abstract.description: True for a generic-input dispatch umbrella cap: a valid alias target never backed by a cartridge and never a runnable graph edge; the capdag CLI narrows it to a concrete specialization by the detected input media. Absent ⇒ false.

args.description: Capability arguments with sources - media_urn is the unique identifier

outputs.description: The outputs the cap gives. Exactly one is the main output, whose media_urn is the cap URN's out=; a cap whose out= is media:void declares none (RULE21). Each output has its own response stream.

metadata_json.description: Arbitrary metadata as JSON object for application-specific use

registered_by.description: Registration attribution - who registered this capability and when

username.description: Username of the user who registered this capability

registered_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the capability was registered (format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)

dim_ref.description: One dim a definition was built from, and the value chosen from it

value.description: The name of the value chosen from that dim

cap_output.description: Output definition - media_urn is the unique identifier

media_urn.description: Unique media URN for this output among the cap's outputs (RULE20). The main output's is the cap URN's out=.

name.description: The label a machine takes this output by. Unique among the cap's outputs, and never true, false or null (RULE19). A label only: the media_urn identifies the output.

optional.description: Whether the cap may end without producing this output (true), in which case what needs it is skipped, or always produces it (false, default)

carries.description: What the output carries when that is not its own media_urn: 'input' is the main input's runtime type, unchanged. Only an output other than the main one, of a cap that takes an input, may declare it (RULE22).

is_sequence.description: Whether this output produces a sequence of items (true) or a single item (false, default)

streaming.description: Whether this output MAY be emitted without a length promise (an unbounded stream: open-ended capture, transcription of one, a generator). false (default) is a contract — every stream is bounded — audited at receipt. Orthogonal to is_sequence.

cap_arg.description: Argument definition - media_urn is the unique identifier

media_urn.description: Unique media URN for this argument (e.g., 'media:enc=utf-8;file-path')

name.description: The label a machine selects this argument by. Unique among the cap's arguments, and never true, false or null (RULE17). A label only: the media_urn identifies the argument.

accepts.description: The media URN this argument's stream must conform to, when that is not its own media_urn. Never beside a stdin source, which says the same for the main input (RULE18). It is what lets two arguments take values of one type.

is_sequence.description: Whether this argument carries a sequence of items (true) or a single item (false, default)

streaming.description: Whether this argument is consumed WITHOUT a length promise — incrementally as the stream arrives (true) — or only as a complete value (false, default). Only the main input may stream (RULE14). Orthogonal to is_sequence.

sources.description: How this argument can be provided (stdin, position, cli_flag)

arg_source.description: Source specification for argument input - must have exactly one of: stdin, position, cli_flag
